extracted.intended_audience: graduate students and advanced undergraduates learning algebraic geometry (readers of Ravi Vakil's 'The Rising Sea')
extracted.subtask_description: Criteria and equivalent formulations for a line bundle (invertible sheaf) to be very ample, ample, semiample or base-point-free on schemes (relative and absolute), together with related preservation and construction results (pullback, tensor products, product schemes) and representability criteria for the Grassmannian functor.

rubrics_metrics.name: Very ample over A (π-very ample / relatively very ample)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L on X (with structure morphism π : X → Spec A) is very ample over A if X ≅ Proj S for some finitely generated graded A-algebra S generated in degree 1, and L ≅ O_Proj S(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Often abbreviated 'very ample' when the structure morphism is clear. Existence of a very ample line bundle implies X is projective. (Definition 4.5.6 referenced.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Equivalent characterization of very ample via global sections
rubrics_metrics.description: L is very ample over A iff there exist finitely many global sections s0,...,sn of L with no common zeros such that the morphism [s0,...,sn] : X → P^n_A is a closed embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given as an 'easy but important exercise' (16.2.A). This is the practical criterion often used to produce embeddings into projective space.

rubrics_metrics.name: Very ample implies base-point-free
rubrics_metrics.description: If L is very ample on a proper A-scheme X then L is base-point-free: for every point p ∈ X there exists a global section of L not vanishing at p.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.2.B; immediate consequence of having a global embedding given by sections with no common zeros.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensoring a very ample with a base-point-free gives very ample
rubrics_metrics.description: If L and M are invertible sheaves on a proper A-scheme X with L very ample over A and M base-point-free, then L ⊗ M is very ample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.2.C. Hint: use the morphism given by M to P^m, take product with embedding from L to P^n and use the Segre embedding plus the Cancellation Theorem for closed embeddings to produce a closed embedding from X into projective space.

rubrics_metrics.name: External product of very ample line bundles is very ample
rubrics_metrics.description: If X and Y are proper A-schemes and L (on X) and M (on Y) are very ample invertible sheaves, then π_X^* L ⊗ π_Y^* M is very ample on X ×_A Y.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.2.D; uses projections and the Segre embedding (cf. Example 15.2.11).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of ample (relative over A)
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L on a proper A-scheme X is (relatively) ample if it satisfies any of the equivalent conditions listed in Theorem 16.2.2 (projective geometry / global generation / topology formulations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The page gives multiple equivalent formulations; see separate rubric entries for each formulation below. Ampleness is weaker but better-behaved than very ampleness in families.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampleness — projective formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: (a) There exists N>0 such that L^{⊗N} is very ample over A. (a') For all n ≫ 0, L^{⊗n} is very ample over A.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One of the equivalent characterizations of ampleness (Theorem 16.2.2). (a') is a stronger-looking but equivalent asymptotic statement when (a) and the other criteria hold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampleness — asymptotic global generation formulation
rubrics_metrics.description: (b) For every finite type quasi-coherent sheaf F on X there exists n0 such that for all n ≥ n0, F ⊗ L^{⊗n} is globally generated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the 'Serre-type' condition (Theorem 16.2.2(b)). It makes no reference to the structure morphism and is used in many arguments (Serre's Theorem A is an immediate corollary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampleness — topology / sections give basis
rubrics_metrics.description: (c) As f runs over global sections of L^{⊗n} for all n>0, the open subsets X_f = {p ∈ X : f(p) ≠ 0} form a basis for the topology of X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Variants: (c') those X_f which are affine form a basis; (c'') those affine X_f cover X. (Theorem 16.2.2(c),(c'),(c'')). These formulations are useful because they avoid reference to π and tie ampleness to generating affine opens by sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences: existence of N making L^N very ample and Serre-related corollaries
rubrics_metrics.description: If (b) and (a) hold then one can choose N so that L^{⊗N} is very ample; Serre's Theorem A and other cohomological consequences follow.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The equivalence (a)⇔(b) is used to derive many standard facts: e.g., if L is ample then L^{⊗n} ⊗ M is very ample for n≫0 (Exercise 16.2.E).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampleness preserved by tensoring with sufficiently high power (making tensors very ample)
rubrics_metrics.description: If L is ample on a proper A-scheme X and M is any invertible sheaf, then for n ≫ 0 the line bundle L^{⊗n} ⊗ M is very ample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.2.E. Hint: use both (a) and (b) of Theorem 16.2.2 and earlier tensor-product exercises.

rubrics_metrics.name: Any line bundle on a projective A-scheme is difference of two very ample bundles
rubrics_metrics.description: For any invertible sheaf L on a projective A-scheme X there exist very ample invertible sheaves M and N with L ≅ M ⊗ N^∨.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.2.F. Use exercise 16.2.E to produce the necessary very ample factors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pullback of an ample bundle under a finite morphism is ample
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → Y is a finite morphism of proper A-schemes and L is ample on Y, then π^* L is ample on X.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.2.G. Use the topology/affine-cover criterion (16.2.2(c'')) to pullback affine opens generated by sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensoring an ample bundle with an ample or base-point-free bundle yields ample
rubrics_metrics.description: If L is ample and M is either ample or base-point-free on a proper A-scheme X, then L ⊗ M is ample.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.2.H; a standard stability property of ampleness under tensor products with 'positive' bundles.

rubrics_metrics.name: Semiample
rubrics_metrics.description: An invertible sheaf L is semiample if some tensor power L^{⊗N} is base-point-free (i.e., gives a morphism to projective space, not necessarily an embedding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 16.2.4. Distinguish semiample (morphism to projective space) from ample (some power gives a closed embedding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampleness in the absolute setting (quasicompact schemes)
rubrics_metrics.description: On a quasicompact scheme X, L is ample iff (variants of Theorem 16.2.6): (b) X quasiseparated and for every finite type quasicoherent sheaf F there exists n0 with F ⊗ L^{⊗n} globally generated for n ≥ n0; (c),(c'),(c'') as in the relative case; (d) letting S = ⊕_{n≥0} Γ(X,L^{⊗n}), the homogeneous positive-degree elements produce opens X_f that cover X and X → Proj S is an open embedding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Warning: S may not be finitely generated. Part (d) implies X is separated. See also 16.2.5 and 16.2.6 for details and variants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stability of ampleness under restriction to closed subschemes and powers
rubrics_metrics.description: For a fixed positive integer n, L is ample iff L^{⊗n} is ample. If Z ↪ X is a closed embedding and L is ample on X, then L|_Z is ample on Z.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.2.J. Useful when passing to subschemes or rescaling powers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ampleness is an open condition in families
rubrics_metrics.description: If π : X → T is a finitely presented proper morphism and L an invertible sheaf on X, then the points t ∈ T where L|_{X_t} is ample form an open subset of T; on that open subset L is relatively ample over the base.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Statement referenced (from EGA) but proof omitted in the text; useful for deformation/parameter-space arguments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projectivity via very ample line bundle
rubrics_metrics.description: A scheme X is projective over A if and only if there exists a very ample invertible sheaf L on X (equivalently an embedding X ↪ P^n_A given by global sections of some power of L).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used repeatedly: existence of very ample implies projective; conversely projective schemes admit O(1).

rubrics_metrics.name: Criterion: cover of X by affine opens X_f produced by sections (use to prove ampleness/projectivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: If positive-degree homogeneous elements f of the graded ring S = ⊕_{n≥0} Γ(X,L^{⊗n}) produce affine opens X_f that cover X and the map X → Proj S is an open (and hence locally closed) embedding, then some further argument (image of proper is proper) gives that X is projective (closed embedding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used in proofs: show (c'') ⇒ (a) by constructing finite affine cover of X by D(b_i) and producing a base-point-free linear series that gives a closed embedding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grassmannian functor representability (general representability criterion used)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Grassmannian functor G(k,n) (sending a scheme B to rank-k locally free quotients of O_B^{⊕n} up to iso) is representable because it is a Zariski sheaf covered by open subfunctors G(k,n)_I (I a k-subset) on which the corresponding k sections are linearly independent; each such open subfunctor is isomorphic to an affine space A^{k(n-k)}.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercises 16.4.A–C give the construction: trivialize Q locally, interpret the surjection as an n×k matrix, take locus where the determinant of the I-columns is nowhere zero, produce coordinates a_{ij} giving maps to affine space. Use Key Exercise 10.1.H to reduce to representability of these opens.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universal exact sequence (tautological bundles) on the Grassmannian
rubrics_metrics.description: Over the Grassmannian there is a tautological short exact sequence 0 → S → O^{⊕n} → Q → 0 where Q is the tautological quotient bundle (rank k) and S the tautological subbundle (rank n−k).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This universal sequence characterizes points of the Grassmannian and is central to further constructions (e.g., Chern classes, Plücker embedding).

rubrics_metrics.name: Plücker embedding criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Applying ∧^k to the tautological surjection O^{⊕n} → Q yields a surjection ∧^k O^{⊕n} → det Q, which corresponds to a morphism P : G(k,n) → P^{(n choose k)-1} (the Plücker embedding).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.4.D: this is the standard way to embed the Grassmannian into projective space; coordinates x_I correspond to determinants of the I-minors of the matrix representing the quotient.

rubrics_metrics.name: Projective coordinates on Grassmannian via determinants
rubrics_metrics.description: The projective coordinate x_I on P^{(n choose k)-1} (coming from the Plücker map) can be interpreted as the determinant of the restricted map φ_I : O^{⊕k} → Q corresponding to the chosen I subset of summands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exercise 16.4.E: makes the Plücker coordinates concrete and ties them to the open covers G(k,n)_I where the I-minor determinant is invertible.
